message.content:
{
  "decision": "APPLY",
  "workflow_yaml": "name: Engineering quality

on:
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]
  push:
    branches: [main]

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  guardrails:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: "3.11"
      - uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v5
      - name: Cache uv dependencies
        uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: ~/.cache/uv
          key: ${{ runner.os }}-uv-${{ hashFiles('uv.lock') }}
          restore-keys: |
            ${{ runner.os }}-uv-
      - name: Install development environment
        run: make install-dev
      - name: Check formatting
        run: make format-check
      - name: Lint
        run: make lint
      - name: Check typed tooling
        run: make typecheck
      - name: Check architecture boundaries
        run: make architecture-check
      - name: Run integration tests
        run: make test-integration
      - name: Run end-to-end tests
        run: make test-e2e
      - name: Validate package artifacts
        run: make package-check",
  "rationale": "The workflow runs uv sync --all-extras --group dev on every pull request and push, repeatedly downloading dependencies while the repository pins them in uv.lock. Adding a GitHub Actions dependency cache for ~/.cache/uv, keyed on the uv.lock hash with runner.os restore keys, matches the P-LIT-GHA-CACHE dependency-download caching pattern, which has measured CI savings. All existing build and test steps are preserved unchanged, and no new permissions, secrets, publishing operations, or network access are introduced.",
  "evidence_ids": ["experiment:batch-interactive-three--f6d2974a5cef7cc9"]
}
